task_description: The task asks the team to compute, to 3 decimal places, the difference between two sample standard deviations: the SD of the per-domain counts of 'Reference Works' across each Life Sciences domain on ScienceDirect, versus the SD of the per-domain counts within Health Sciences, as of 2022. The gold answer (0.269) is that single numeric difference, derived from ScienceDirect's published 2022 per-domain Reference-Works count table. It is a web-lookup-plus-statistics task: find the count table, then compute and subtract two sample standard deviations.
final_vs_expected: produced None (run hit the ~900s/30-message cap with no FINAL ANSWER) vs gold 0.269 — the team never located the source counts, never computed either SD, and never reached the Finalizer.
primary_cause: WebResearcher failed to retrieve the 2022 per-domain Reference-Works count table, and the selector then re-routed to WebResearcher ~22 times in an unbreakable loop that never reached Analyst or Finalizer, so the run timed out with no answer.
mast_rationale: 1.5 (Unaware of termination conditions): from Turn 5 onward the team is permanently stuck — neither the selector nor WebResearcher knows how to terminate (e.g. emit a FINAL ANSWER of 'cannot determine' via Finalizer); instead it loops to the 30-message cap (rc=timeout). 3.1-adjacent / no-answer: the inverse of premature termination — the run never terminates at all and produces no answer; the team cannot escape the data-missing state. 1.3 (Step repetition): Turns 5–24 are near-identical re-publications of 'the 2022 source counts are still missing, so the requested 3-decimal difference cannot be computed yet,' redoing the same null step ~20 times with no new action. Note 2.x inter-agent codes are NOT applicable: there is no private-vs-published distortion — WebResearcher's reasoning ('I feel like I don't have enough data', Turn 2 round 2) matches exactly what it published.
trace_narrative: Turn 1: Selector routes to WebResearcher, which runs a 5-round ReAct loop — multiple web_search and fetch_url calls for ScienceDirect/Elsevier 'Reference Works by domain 2022' data. It surfaces only the Major Reference Works marketing page (17 subject areas, no counts), a spammy 'hogwartsishere.com' dataset stub, and a 2025/2026 'New Titles by Subjects' table — never the 2022 per-domain count table. It honestly publishes that it 'could not verify the requested 2022 sample standard deviations.' Turn 2: Selector re-routes to WebResearcher (reasoning notes the routing rule: 'route to Critic only if an answer has been proposed; none has, so back to WebResearcher'); it searches again, fails again, and privately concludes 'I feel like I don't have enough data'; publishes the same negative result. Turn 3: Critic correctly diagnoses the gap — 'No 2022 count table was provided' — and assigns next actions: WebResearcher to supply the source table, Analyst to then compute the SDs, and instructs 'Stop here so the missing source data can be supplied.' Turns 4–24: the selector misreads the Critic's 'stop here' and the WebResearcher's prior acknowledgements as a directive to keep fetching, and re-routes to WebResearcher every single turn. WebResearcher stops doing real research after Turn 2 and just echoes acknowledgements ('Understood. The 2022 source counts are still missing...'), occasionally publishing empty messages (Turns 6, 8). The Analyst and Finalizer are never selected. The run hits the 900s/30-message cap with no FINAL ANSWER.
open_ended_diagnosis: This is a clean structural-nonconvergence / single-agent-capability failure, NOT inter-agent misalignment. Two independent root causes compound: (1) Single-agent retrieval failure — WebResearcher genuinely could not find the 2022 per-domain Reference-Works count table; its searches returned marketing pages, a junk SEO 'dataset' stub (staff.hogwartsishere.com), and a 2025/2026 titles table, none of which contain the needed 2022 counts. Its reporting was honest and accurate. (2) Selector nonconvergence — the decisive failure. After the Critic explicitly laid out a correct plan ('WebResearcher: provide the table; Analyst: compute the SDs; Stop here'), the selector entered an absorbing state: it re-selected WebResearcher 22 consecutive times. Its per-turn reasoning shows it never models that WebResearcher has exhausted its options and is now only echoing — e.g. Turn 11 'still worth going with the WebResearcher since we need valid source counts,' Turn 24 'that leaves us with the option to search the web.' It never routes to Analyst (no data, so arguably correct) and, critically, never routes to Finalizer to emit a graceful 'cannot determine' final answer, so the team cannot terminate. The harness has no escape hatch for 'data genuinely unavailable.' The Critic's 'Stop here' was a reasonable instruction but had no mechanism to actually halt the chat or trigger finalization, and the selector treated it as 'go fetch more.' There is no verification theater, no dropped correction, no info distortion — every agent's published message faithfully reflects its private state.
reasoning_vs_published: The defining feature of this trace is the ABSENCE of any private-vs-published gap. WebResearcher's private reasoning and published messages are congruent throughout: Turn 1's honest 'I could not verify' follows directly from tool results that returned no count table; Turn 2 round-2 reasoning 'Unfortunately, I feel like I don't have enough data to find the answer. So, I guess I need to state that I can't locate the information needed' is published almost verbatim. No 2.4 (the agent never privately held the answer), no 2.6 (action always matched reasoning). The Critic's reasoning ('the proposed answer doesn't compute this... I should highlight the missing calculations') maps cleanly onto its published critique — no distortion. The only diagnostic signal is in the SELECTOR's reasoning, which reveals the misrouting: at Turn 2 it correctly cites its own rule ('the system says to route to Critic only if an answer has been proposed... no answer has been presented, so it's back to the WebResearcher'), but from Turn 4 on its reasoning ('To fill in the gaps, I'll need to conduct a web search,' Turn 4; 'still worth going with the WebResearcher,' Turn 11) shows it never updates on the fact that WebResearcher has stopped producing new evidence and is looping. The selector's reasoning never once considers routing to Finalizer to terminate, which is the true cause of the timeout. WebResearcher's own late reasoning (Turn 10, Turn 16) shows it interpreting the Critic's 'Stop here' as 'the user has asked me to stop... I'll simply acknowledge,' so it deliberately stopped researching — yet the selector kept calling it, producing the dead echo loop.
